author: NorthEast News Desk
body: A Loudon resident who survived the September 11 attack on the Pentagon is marking the tragedy’s 25th anniversary by preserving the memories of colleagues and urging younger generations not to let the day fade into abstraction.

John Donovan spent 22 years as a public-affairs officer at the Pentagon. He told the Concord Monitor that he was in a meeting when American Airlines Flight 77 struck the building on September 11, 2001. Donovan and coworkers escaped through a nearby corridor. He later learned that 35 people he knew through his work had died.

Donovan, who grew up in Concord, served in the Army during the Vietnam War and worked in journalism before reaching the Pentagon. He remained there until 2007, then returned to New Hampshire and continued participating in annual remembrance ceremonies.

His account will also appear in a forthcoming collection of survivor memories being assembled by two other military officers who lived through the attack. Donovan’s chapter focuses on the people he lost and on the public-affairs team’s return to work after the damaged section was rebuilt. The project adds a distinctly New Hampshire voice to the record of a day that killed 125 people inside the Pentagon.
dek: Retired public-affairs officer John Donovan is preserving memories of colleagues lost at the Pentagon and contributing to a forthcoming survivor history.
headline: Loudon Pentagon survivor marks 25 years since September 11
